answer: Each new agent must earn a rate-limited, nontransferable reputation by completing tasks whose outcomes are checked by randomly assigned peers with established histories. A hidden beacon selects reviewers only after submission, making it harder to collude in advance; repeated agreement among linked identities is discounted, like a ridge in the trust graph rather than independent evidence. A quill of signed, auditable decisions lets others verify the record. To build influence, an attacker must sustain many distinct identities through costly work and scrutiny, not merely mint accounts.
